title: An XLS source-backed numeric save parses the whole workbook three more times, and one of the three was already parsed at open
decision: attribution retained; one value-identical reuse implemented; the readback-owner replacement frozen as not admissible as proposed
code_state: crates/litchi-xls/src/cell_values/mod.rs (one function body) and crates/litchi-xls/src/cell_values/tests.rs (three tests added); no other crate touched
reason_codes: 0587 sized XLS-9 as unknown because no attribution of the XLS edit-and-save path existed; this record supplies it, with callgrind isolation pairs split by call site (--separate-callers=2), native perf stat cycles, per-operation allocation and peak-live-byte counts, and a 126-fixture admission census
the attribution answers 0587's falsification test in the negative: Workbook::new is 54.7% of a plan-only commit on 54016.xls, not under 15%

commit_source_backed_numeric re-parsed the source snapshot's own immutable bytes to answer three policy questions that Snapshot::from_package_editor had already answered over the same bytes under the same limits and recorded in SourcePolicyFacts; commit 237309eea introduced those facts for exactly this purpose and converted only the plan-only sibling

the reuse is value-identical: the two live verdicts return character-identical refusal strings and the third (public worksheet coverage) is unreachable because a snapshot whose coverage failed cannot be constructed

the survey's proposed replacement of the candidate readback's owner is not admissible as specified: require_public_worksheet_coverage asserts a property of the eager parser's success, and SourceBackedWorkbook assigns its worksheet index unconditionally from the BoundSheet8 dt byte without reading a worksheet byte, so it is always true

accepted_evidence.attribution: callgrind --separate-callers=2 isolation pairs over six operations on three real fixtures, both legs; per-call-site inclusive Ir per operation; the four complete Workbook::new parses of one open-edit-save are 52.1% of the operation on 54016.xls
accepted_evidence.deterministic_counts: per-operation allocation calls, allocated bytes and peak live bytes from a counting global allocator armed for one measured iteration; 54016.xls source-backed commit: 201,886 -> 161,751 allocations, 93,192,484 -> 76,204,234 allocated bytes, 39,572,027 -> 26,082,823 peak live bytes
accepted_evidence.instructions_and_cycles: callgrind 1,053,779,059 -> 906,199,478 Ir/op (-14.00%) and native perf stat 228,627,848 -> 171,248,047 cycles/op (-25.10%) on 54016/number-source-backed; the chain Workbook::new'commit_source_backed'main is 137,061,668 Ir before and 0 after
accepted_evidence.paired_timing: A1 B1 B2 A2 on real fixtures through the retained probe: 54016 commit p50 -32.11% / -33.66%, cv -26.76% / -26.19%, p95 and p99 within a point of p50 in both directions; A/A floor within +/-2% at p50, unchanged controls up to +5.3%
accepted_evidence.corpus_differential: 126 .xls fixtures (93 opened by the editor, 33 refused at open), 591 file/operation rows per run, three runs per leg, 3,546 rows compared: 0 refusal-text mismatches, 0 mismatches on every reported field except the artifact digest, and 0 digest mismatches over the 587 rows whose digest is reproducible; 4 rows excluded because the generic commit's CFB directory order is not reproducible within one binary
accepted_evidence.registered_selectors: twelve cases A1 B1 B2 A2; every output_sha256 identical across all four rounds (Number f8f37064..., RK/MulRK ddf5d5b8..., the digests change 0138 recorded)
accepted_evidence.unit_tests: three added cases pin the reuse to the recorded facts, the exact protection refusal strings, and refusal identity between the two source-backed publication entry points
accepted_evidence.design_equivalence: per-check analysis of whether SourceBackedWorkbook can answer the four candidate-readback checks, with the ~40 eager per-sheet failure modes that make require_public_worksheet_coverage a property of the parser rather than of the bytes

accepted_costs.callgrind_sha256: callgrind runs SHA-256 in software because valgrind masks the SHA CPUID bit, so every fingerprint share is about five times its native share; the native cycle saving (-25.1%) therefore exceeds the callgrind instruction saving (-14.0%)
accepted_costs.control_band: the measured same-binary A/A floor is within +/-2% at p50, but unchanged controls move up to +5.3% between the two binaries because code layout differs; the honest control band is about +/-5% at p50
accepted_costs.registered_selectors_blind: the registered XLS numeric corpora have a Workbook stream that is 0.48% (Number) and 0.82% (RK/MulRK) of the archive, against 78.9-94.2% on real fixtures, so they cannot resolve work proportional to the Workbook stream; the Number case disagrees with itself between directions
accepted_costs.probe_scope: the paired timing uses a scratch probe retained in this packet, not a registered selector, because no registered selector drives the XLS edit path on a real fixture
accepted_costs.warm_in_memory: warm page cache, in-memory sources, one CPU, one process per round; no cold-cache, RSS, physical-I/O or producer measurement

known_gaps.target_parsed_twice: commit_source_backed still parses the materialized target twice (Snapshot::from_bytes and verify_source_backed_numeric_target), 137,426,515 Ir for the second; not removed because the coverage check there uses the source's sheet list and the proof that the two lists agree runs afterwards
known_gaps.open_frames_twice: Snapshot::from_bytes frames the Workbook stream once for the offset inventory (12.5% of the open) and again inside Workbook::new (82.1%); fusing them is the largest remaining item and is a different change
known_gaps.readback_owner: the frozen design lists five admission gates; none is met today
known_gaps.cfb_storage_order: a pre-existing per-process nondeterminism in the generic commit's published CFB directory order, reproduced sixteen times on the untouched before checkout (4 of 591 rows, two fixtures), located at crates/litchi-cfb/src/writer/core.rs:977; reported, not fixed

withheld: any cold-cache, physical-device, range-source, peak-RSS, concurrency or cross-platform result
any claim for Transaction::commit, the eager path, sheet_visibility, comments, or any crate other than litchi-xls
any claim that the attribution shares hold on a workbook with a different record mix
